sections.heading: Answering the phone
sections.body:
How people answer varies by country: *¿Aló?* (much of South America), *¿Bueno?* (Mexico), *¿Diga? / ¿Dígame?* (Spain, also formal), *¿Hola?* (Argentina and many others). The caller says who they are: *Hola, soy Clara* or *Habla Clara* (Clara speaking).

- *¿Está Luis?* / *¿Se encuentra el señor Díaz?* — Is Luis / Mr. Díaz there?
- *¿De parte de quién?* — Who's calling?
- *Un momento, por favor.* / *No cuelgue.* — Hold on. / Don't hang up.
- *No está. ¿Quiere dejar un mensaje?* — He's not here. Would you like to leave a message?
- *¿Le puede decir que me llame?* — Can you tell him to call me? (subjunctive — you'll learn why in B1)
- *Se cortó.* — The call dropped. *Te escucho mal.* — I can't hear you well.

sections.heading: Making plans: quedar
sections.body:
In much of the Spanish-speaking world, *quedar* means "to arrange to meet": *¿Quedamos el sábado?* (Shall we meet on Saturday?) *Quedé con Ana a las ocho.* (I arranged to meet Ana at eight.) In many Latin American countries people also say *¿Nos vemos el sábado?* or *¿Nos juntamos?* (Chile, Argentina).

- *¿Dónde quedamos? / ¿Dónde nos vemos?* — Where shall we meet?
- *¿Te viene bien a las siete?* / *¿Te queda bien…?* — Does seven work for you?
- *Mejor a las ocho.* — Better at eight.
- *Perfecto, nos vemos allí.* — Perfect, see you there.

sections.heading: Messages
sections.body: Texting (*mandar un mensaje*, *escribir por WhatsApp* — often just *te escribo*) is everywhere. Common abbreviations: *q* (que), *xq* (porque / por qué), *tb* (también), *bs* (besos), *jaja* (haha).

examples: Un momento, por favor. No cuelgue.
One moment, please. Don't hang up.
He's not here. Would you like to leave a message?
Dígale que me devuelva la llamada, por favor.
Please tell him to call me back.
Quedé con Ana a las ocho.
I arranged to meet Ana at eight.
Tengo una cita con el médico.
I'll call you when I get there.
